answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock 100 credits for a 30-day horizon before its ratings count. Splitting one balance among nebula, nectar, and a thousand other aliases creates no extra voting weight: each counted rating needs its own fully funded bond. The marginal cost of another active fake is therefore 100 credits tied up for 30 days, plus the financing cost of that capital; an attacker cannot recycle one bond across simultaneous identities.
